#### 8.6 Switching Between PWM / Thermal relay and SMBus communication

8.6.1. PWM is enabled

The diagram below illustrates the way of switching to SMBus if PWM / Thermal Relay is enabled (factory programmed POR default for MLX90614 is SMBus, PWM disabled). Note that the SCL pin needs to be kept high in order to use PWM.

Figure 19: Request (switch to SMBus) condition

If PWM / Thermal relay is enabled, the MLX90614's SMBus Request condition is needed to disable PWM / Thermal relay and reconfigure PWM/SDA pin before starting SMBus communication. Once PWM / Thermal relay is disabled, it can be only enabled by switching the supply OFF – ON or exit from Sleep Mode. The MLX90614's SMBus request condition requires forcing LOW the SCL pin for period longer than the request time (\(t_{req1}\))>.1 for \(4ms\). The SDA line value is ignored and is irrelevant in this case.

8.6.3. PWM is disabled

If PWM is disabled by means of EEPROM the PWM / SDA pin is directly used for the SMBus after POR. Request condition should not be sent in this case.

}^1 measurements are available.The algorithm works by alternately generating a set of PWBMs, measuring their 99th percentile values, and evaluating whether or not they fall below a threshold. If a PWBMA (PICA Weighted Boundary Model) meets the threshold (i.e., output set m), it undergoes a delay of one sample before allowing the next step.A weight vector \((Y_t^n \in \mathbb{R}^{\frac{R}{2}}^m, t = 1,2,\dots,T)\) is constructed based on the thresholds \(i = 2\cdots n\). This vector reflects the subjective opinion on the safety of a particular PWBMA \(Y_t^{n}\). The set of thresholds \((Y_t^n)\) is divided into intervals \((Y_{t,j}^{n}, j = 1,2,\dots,F)\) containing the thresholds \(i = 2\dots n\). Simplified thresholds \(Y_{1,j}^{n}\) are defined as follows:
\[Y_{1,j}^{n} = 
\begin{cases} 
1, & \text{if }[m_{1,j},m_{2,j}] \cap Y_{t, j-1}^{n} \neq \varnothing \\ 
0, & \text{otherwise} 
\end{cases}\]
Transmission lift measurements, \(\overline{T}_{t,j}^n\), are also generated for the same interval, \(j\) and \(t\). A message \(m_{1, j}^{n}\) is provided. The resulting values \(T_{Di \cdot n}\) are sorted in ascending order and the new intervals \(R_{D i,n}\) are determined. If the threshold \(i\) is equal to \(R_{D i, n - 1}\), a new interval is created and given the threshold \(i\cdot \text{bias}\) is added to \(i\). If \(\overline{T}_{D i \cdot n}\) essentially equals the simulated full-scale load \(q\), it must be set to the PWBMA result and its weight must be greater than 2. A new transmission delay \(T_{O,i,n}\) for option \(i\) is computed and the comparison of the weighted delays with a threshold is evaluated. In the case of no violation, \(TR\ needsEntries\), is preserved by writing the new set of thresholds \(\left(T_{p o l l a b}\right)\) for option \(i\). ### 8. Calculation Process

1. **Initialization**: Constants such as the offset mean and I-R offset mean are initialized.
2. **Selection of PWB**: The PWB with the largest 99th percentile weight is selected.
3. **Multiplication with Offset MAP**: For each rated operation moment \(m = 1,2,\cdots, M\):
   - The PWB with the smallest 99th percentile weight is multiplied by \(1\) if \(m\) is a rated operation moment.
   - The rest stored weights are reduced by \(1\).
   - Through the above operation, the PWB with the smallest 99th percentile weight is selected.
   - The multiplication is essential for obtaining safe PWBMA weights for "embarrassment" or control signals at rating.
4. **SSD for Each Rated Operation**: An SSD is computed based on the nearest PWBmax, the weights stored previously (and their scales constant thus not shown).
   - If the PWBmax is not the same for all rated operation moments, the operand solution is chosen based only on the highest weight.

Version MLX90614ESF-DCC, -DCH and -DCI comply with ASTM standard section 5.4 (Designation: E1965 – 98 (Re-approved 2009) -Standard Specification for Infrared Thermometers for Intermittent Determination of Patient Temperature.

It is very important for the application designer to understand that the accuracy specified in Figure 22 and Figure 24 are only guaranteed when the sensor is in thermal equilibrium and under isothermal conditions (there are no temperature differences across the sensor package). The accuracy of the thermometer can be influenced by temperature differences in the package induced by causes like (among others): Hot electronics (heaters / coolers) behind or beside the sensor or when the measured object is so close to the sensor that heats the thermometer package.

This effect is especially relevant for thermometers with a small Field Of View (FOV) like the xxC and xxF as the energy received by the sensor from the object is reduced. Therefore, Melexis has introduced the xxC version of the MLX90614. In these MLX90614xCx, the thermal gradients are measured internally and the measured temperature is compensated for them. In this way, the MLX90614xCx is much less sensitive to thermal gradients induced from outside, but the effect is not totally eliminated. It is therefore important to avoid introducing strong heat sources close to the sensor or to shield the sensor from them.

NOTE: In order to have the highest possible signal and the best performance a higher gain of the amplifier is selected for MLX90614DCx type of devices. This eventually would limit the maximum object temperature (due to overload of the ADC) to about 200°C.

## 10.1.3 Temperature reading.dependence on dD
 
In case of medical applications where high accuracy is required and the supply is provided by means of a battery, a compensation of temperature readings from VDD dependence should be done by the microcontroller. The dependence is very repeatable and compensation can easily be implemented. As this dependence comes from the ambient temperature it is the same for all type of devices regardless of FOV and optics used and it directly translates in the same compensation for object temperature.
The typical VDD dependence of the ambient and object temperature is **0.6°C/V**.
